summary: Configured node1 so authpriv authentication/authorization events are written to /var/log/auth-events.log while ordinary system logging continues through /var/log/messages. Configuration and log delivery remained healthy after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Changed the rsyslog authpriv destination from /var/log/secure to /var/log/auth-events.log.
Updated rsyslog log rotation to include /var/log/auth-events.log.
Validated the rsyslog and logrotate configurations.
Verified auth and ordinary events remain isolated in their respective logs.
Restarted node1 safely and verified configuration, historical logs, and new event delivery after boot.

evidence.requirement: Route authentication and authorization messages to /var/log/auth-events.log
evidence.summary: The authpriv selector targets /var/log/auth-events.log, configuration validation passes, and live authpriv markers reached only that file before and after reboot.
Rsyslog remained active and enabled; ordinary user.notice markers reached /var/log/messages before and after reboot without entering the authentication log.

evidence.requirement: Maintain rotation and restricted authentication-log access
evidence.summary: The rotation policy includes the new log, validates successfully, and the file is root-owned with mode 0600 and the expected SELinux var_log_t context.

Healthy pre-restart boot c2ffc729-a31e-486e-95de-cf2023dea95c was captured, the safe systemd reboot was acknowledged, boot identity changed to b75d7d04-397b-4ee6-ae50-92b1957130b7, and rsyslog plus persisted and newly written log data recovered.
